title: Unified retry policy, idempotency keys, and retryable error taxonomy for SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and land a cross-SDK default retry/backoff policy, a consistent idempotency key scheme, and a retryable error taxonomy that SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) implement. This ticket captures the spec, examples, tests, and rollout plan so product teams can rely on uniform behavior across languages.
background: We currently have ad-hoc retry behavior across SDKs. Differences in default retries, backoff, and how idempotency keys are exposed cause customer confusion, subtle duplicate side-effects (charges, resource creation), and make debugging incidents harder. A single spec will reduce incidents, improve ergonomics for users implementing retries, and simplify server-side idempotency support.
proposal_summary: Standardize a conservative default: 3 total attempts (1 initial + 2 retries), exponential backoff with multiplier 2.0, initial backoff 100ms, max backoff 2000ms, full jitter. Expose idempotency key header 'Idempotency-Key' with SDK helpers to auto-generate language-prefixed v4 UUID keys and an optional 'Idempotency-Attempt' header that increments per try. Define clear retryable error classes (transient, rate-limit, and server-error) and non-retryable classes (client errors, validation). Provide concrete usage examples and a migration plan for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: RFC merged in repos/sdk-specs outlining policy and headers
Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs implement defaults and surface opt-out/config parameters
Automated unit + integration tests validate retry behavior against mocked transient and permanent errors
End-to-end examples in docs for idempotent create flows and streaming nuances
Rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry to monitor retry rates and failure modes
implementation_plan: Draft RFC (this ticket) and review with platform and API teams
Implement SDK helpers: IdempotencyKey.generate(language), and client option default_retry_policy
Implement shared retry logic module in each SDK with the same parameter defaults and jitter strategy
Add server-side small change to log Idempotency-Key and Idempotency-Attempt for troubleshooting (coordination with API team)
Add tests and sample apps demonstrating best practices
Feature-flag rollout and monitor metrics for duplicate-operation rates and user complaints
retry_policy_spec: Defaults: max_attempts=3, initial_backoff_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=2000, multiplier=2.0, jitter=full jitter. Behavior: retry only on errors classified as retryable (see taxonomy). Retries are disabled for streaming connections by default; for resumable streams, SDKs will surface resume token support when available.
idempotency_spec: Header: 'Idempotency-Key' (string). SDKs auto-generate keys using 'sdk-{language}-{v4uuid}' when helper used. TTL: server-side recommended 24h. SDKs additionally send 'Idempotency-Attempt' which starts at 1 and increments with each client-initiated retry. Guidance: callers should provide their own stable idempotency key for user-initiated retries (e.g., form submission ID). For non-idempotent streaming or long-running jobs, recommend server-supported resume tokens instead of client-generated keys.
error_taxonomy: retryable_transient: network errors (TCP timeouts, connection reset), DNS failures. retryable_rate_limit: 429 responses; treat as retryable with larger initial backoff and optionally respect 'Retry-After' when present. retryable_server: 500-599 responses except 501/505 which indicate client incompatibility. non_retryable_client: 400-499 except 429. non_retryable_validation: 422 or other schema validation failures. authentication_and_authorization: 401/403 are non-retryable; prompt for credentials/permissions. streaming_specific: streaming responses with partial state are non-retryable unless server provides a resume token endpoint. The taxonomy will be published in SDK docs and used by the SDKs' retry predicate implementations.
cross_sdk_ergonomics: Provide identical public API names where possible: Python: client.with_retries(policy=DefaultRetryPolicy()), TypeScript: client.withRetries({policy: DefaultRetryPolicy}), Go: client.WithRetries(DefaultRetryPolicy()). Provide utility to opt-out (retry_disabled=true) and to override numeric parameters. Provide consistent telemetry fields: retry_attempts, idempotency_key, retry_reason.
code_examples:
Python example:
from redwood import Client, IdempotencyKey, DefaultRetryPolicy
client = Client(api_key=..., retries=DefaultRetryPolicy())
key = IdempotencyKey.generate('python')
resp = client.create_completion(prompt='hi', idempotency_key=key)

Go example:
client := redwood.NewClient(options.WithAPIKey(os.Getenv('RW_KEY')), options.WithRetries(redwood.DefaultRetryPolicy()))
key := idempotency.Generate("go")
resp, err := client.CreateCompletion(context.Background(), &CreateRequest{ Prompt: "hi", IdempotencyKey: key })
streaming_guidance: Default: streaming RPCs are not automatically retried. For server flows that support resume tokens, SDKs will expose a resumable streaming helper that accepts a resume token. For CRITICAL idempotent operations, recommend a non-streaming create followed by a streaming consume pattern where resume semantics are explicit.
testing_plan: Unit tests: retry predicate and backoff math with deterministic jitter seeding
Integration tests: mock server returning transient errors, 429s with Retry-After, and permanent 4xx errors
Chaos test: inject random connection drops in CI to validate idempotency headers and no duplicates
E2E sample app that demonstrates stable idempotency usage and metrics collection
monitoring_and_telemetry: Emit metrics: sdk.retry.attempts, sdk.retry.failures, sdk.retry.duplicate_detected (when server signals duplicate), sdk.idempotency.key_used. Log headers Idempotency-Key and Idempotency-Attempt at info level controlled by debug flag. Set an alert for duplicate-operation-rate > 0.1% for two-week window post rollout.
risks: Server changes required to fully support idempotency headers (coordination risk)
Automatic idempotency keys may give false sense of safety for non-idempotent operations
Edge cases for resumed streaming may lead to inconsistencies if resume tokens misused
